description: Question bank on Continental Drift, Wegener, Pangaea and related topics. Verify and expand questions before formal examination use.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does the continental drift theory state?

options.A: Continents have always been fixed in their present positions
options.B: Continents were once united into a large landmass and gradually moved to their present positions over geological time
options.C: Continents are formed by volcanic eruptions only
options.D: Continents move only vertically up and down

questions.explanation: The continental drift theory states that the continents were once united into a large landmass and gradually moved to their present positions over geological time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Who is credited with proposing the influential modern continental drift hypothesis?

options.A: Harry Hess
options.B: Alfred Lothar Wegener
options.C: Charles Lyell
options.D: James Hutton

questions.explanation: German meteorologist and geophysicist Alfred Lothar Wegener (1880–1930) is credited with proposing the influential modern continental drift hypothesis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which year did Wegener present the continental drift hypothesis?
questions.explanation: Wegener presented the idea in 1912 and developed it in his book The Origin of Continents and Oceans, first published in German in 1915.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which year was the first edition of Wegener's book The Origin of Continents and Oceans published?
questions.explanation: The Origin of Continents and Oceans (German: Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane) was first published in 1915.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What was the central argument of Wegener's theory?

options.A: Continents are permanently fixed
options.B: Continents had once formed a single supercontinent, Pangaea, and subsequently drifted apart
options.C: Ocean floors are stationary
options.D: Continents move only due to earthquakes

questions.explanation: The continents were not permanently fixed. They had once formed a single supercontinent, Pangaea, and subsequently drifted apart to their current positions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does the word 'drift' mean in the continental drift theory?

options.A: Vertical movement of continents
options.B: Long-term horizontal movement of continental landmasses relative to one another across geological time
options.C: Rapid movement of continents during earthquakes
options.D: Movement of ocean water

questions.explanation: It refers to the long-term horizontal movement of continental landmasses relative to one another across geological time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Did Wegener develop the modern theory of plate tectonics?

options.A: Yes, he developed both continental drift and plate tectonics
options.B: No, Wegener proposed continental drift, but modern plate tectonics was developed later
options.C: Yes, he coined the term plate tectonics
options.D: No, he proposed seafloor spreading instead

questions.explanation: Wegener proposed continental drift, but modern plate tectonics was developed later through evidence including seafloor spreading, ocean-floor magnetic patterns, global earthquake distribution and the recognition that rigid lithospheric plates move.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why was continental drift an important scientific idea?

options.A: It proved that continents are fixed
options.B: It challenged the prevailing assumption that continents and ocean basins were essentially fixed
options.C: It explained the origin of the universe
options.D: It supported the geocentric theory

questions.explanation: It challenged the prevailing assumption that continents and ocean basins were essentially fixed. It encouraged scientists to seek explanations for matching coastlines, fossils, rock formations and ancient climatic evidence across oceans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Who was Alfred Lothar Wegener?

options.A: A German scientist (1880–1930) trained in astronomy and known for work in meteorology, geophysics and polar research
options.B: An English geologist who discovered seafloor spreading
options.C: An American physicist who proposed plate tectonics
options.D: A French biologist who studied fossils

questions.explanation: Alfred Lothar Wegener was a German scientist (1880–1930), trained in astronomy and known for work in meteorology, geophysics and polar research. He is best known for formulating the continental drift hypothesis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What was Wegener's professional background by original training?

options.A: Geologist
options.B: Meteorologist
options.C: Astronomer
options.D: Biologist

questions.explanation: Wegener was trained in astronomy. He was a meteorologist by professional background, not a geologist by original training.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What observations led Wegener to propose continental drift?

options.A: Only the study of ocean currents
options.B: The apparent fit of continental margins, similarities in fossils and geological structures on opposite sides of oceans, and evidence of past climates inconsistent with present locations
options.C: Only the study of earthquakes
options.D: Only the study of volcanic eruptions

questions.explanation: He considered the apparent fit of continental margins, similarities in fossils and geological structures on opposite sides of oceans, and evidence of past climates that seemed inconsistent with the continents' present locations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Was Wegener's idea accepted immediately by the scientific community?

options.A: Yes, it was universally accepted
options.B: No, many geologists rejected or criticised it, particularly because he could not provide a convincing physical mechanism
options.C: Yes, but only after 1915
options.D: No, because he had no fossil evidence

questions.explanation: No. Many geologists rejected or criticised it, particularly because he could not provide a convincing physical mechanism capable of moving continents across the ocean floor.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How did Alfred Wegener die?

options.A: He died in 1930 during an expedition to Greenland
options.B: He died in 1915 in Germany
options.C: He died in 1960 in the United States
options.D: He died in 1925 during an expedition to Antarctica

questions.explanation: He died in 1930 during an expedition to Greenland. His death is not evidence for or against the theory, but is a biographical fact sometimes asked in general-knowledge examinations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What was Pangaea?

options.A: A global ocean surrounding all continents
options.B: An ancient supercontinent in which nearly all or most of Earth's present continental landmasses were joined together
options.C: A mid-ocean ridge
options.D: A volcanic island arc

questions.explanation: Pangaea was an ancient supercontinent in which nearly all or most of Earth's present continental landmasses were joined together. The name means 'all Earth' or 'entire Earth'.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does the name 'Pangaea' mean?

options.A: All sea
options.B: All Earth or entire Earth
options.C: Northern land
options.D: Southern land

questions.explanation: The name Pangaea means 'all Earth' or 'entire Earth'.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: When did Pangaea exist?

options.A: It assembled during the late Paleozoic, was present through much of the early Mesozoic, and began breaking apart during the Mesozoic
options.B: It existed only during the Precambrian
options.C: It formed during the Cenozoic and still exists today
options.D: It existed only during the Jurassic period

questions.explanation: Pangaea assembled during the late Paleozoic, was present through much of the early Mesozoic, and began breaking apart during the Mesozoic. The breakup was a prolonged process rather than a single event.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a supercontinent?

options.A: A large ocean
options.B: A large landmass formed when most or nearly all continental blocks are joined together
options.C: A chain of volcanic islands
options.D: A mid-ocean ridge

questions.explanation: A supercontinent is a large landmass formed when most or nearly all continental blocks are joined together.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How did Pangaea begin to break apart?

options.A: Through a single sudden event
options.B: Through rifting and extension that fractured the supercontinent, with the opening of new ocean basins and seafloor spreading progressively separating continental fragments
options.C: Through a meteor impact only
options.D: Through glacial erosion only

questions.explanation: Rifting and extension fractured the supercontinent. The opening of new ocean basins and seafloor spreading progressively separated the continental fragments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What were the two major landmasses formed as Pangaea fragmented?

options.A: Panthalassa and Tethys
options.B: Laurasia and Gondwanaland
options.C: Rodinia and Columbia
options.D: Atlantis and Lemuria

questions.explanation: The northern landmass was Laurasia and the southern landmass was Gondwanaland (also called Gondwana). The Tethys Sea lay between them in simplified reconstructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Was Pangaea the only supercontinent in Earth's history?

options.A: Yes, it was the only one
options.B: No, earlier supercontinents existed, including Rodinia and Columbia/Nuna
options.C: Yes, and it still exists today
options.D: No, but no other supercontinent has been identified

questions.explanation: No. Geological evidence indicates that earlier supercontinents existed, including Rodinia and Columbia/Nuna. Pangaea is especially important in school-level continental-drift study.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What was Panthalassa?

options.A: A supercontinent
options.B: The vast global ocean that surrounded Pangaea
options.C: A mountain range
options.D: A desert region

questions.explanation: Panthalassa was the vast global ocean that surrounded Pangaea. The name is commonly interpreted as 'all sea'.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does the name 'Panthalassa' mean?

options.A: All Earth
options.B: All sea
options.C: Northern land
options.D: Southern land

questions.explanation: The name Panthalassa is commonly interpreted as 'all sea'.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What happened to Panthalassa as Pangaea broke apart?

options.A: It disappeared completely
options.B: As continental fragments separated and new ocean basins opened, the geography of the surrounding oceans changed; the modern Pacific Ocean is commonly described as the principal remnant of Panthalassa
options.C: It became a landmass
options.D: It became the Tethys Sea

questions.explanation: As continental fragments separated and new ocean basins opened, the geography of the surrounding oceans changed. The modern Pacific Ocean is commonly described as the principal remnant of Panthalassa, although the ocean's boundaries and crust have been extensively transformed by plate tectonics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between Panthalassa and the Tethys Sea?

options.A: Panthalassa was the enormous ocean surrounding Pangaea; the Tethys was a major oceanic seaway between Laurasia and Gondwana
options.B: Panthalassa was between Laurasia and Gondwana; the Tethys surrounded Pangaea
options.C: They are the same thing
options.D: Panthalassa was a supercontinent; the Tethys was an ocean

questions.explanation: Panthalassa was the enormous ocean surrounding Pangaea. The Tethys was a major oceanic seaway located between the northern Laurasian and southern Gondwanan landmasses in standard reconstructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What was Laurasia?

options.A: The southern major continental assemblage
options.B: The northern major continental assemblage produced during the breakup of Pangaea
options.C: The vast ocean surrounding Pangaea
options.D: An ancient supercontinent older than Pangaea

questions.explanation: Laurasia was the northern major continental assemblage produced during the breakup of Pangaea. In simplified reconstructions, it included North America and much of Europe and Asia.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which modern continents are mainly associated with Laurasia?

options.A: South America and Africa
options.B: North America and Eurasia (Europe and most of Asia)
options.C: Australia and Antarctica
options.D: India and South America

questions.explanation: North America and Eurasia (Europe and most of Asia) are commonly linked to Laurasia, although the assembly and later fragmentation of these regions involved several smaller terranes and complex tectonic events.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What ocean lay between Laurasia and Gondwanaland?

options.A: Panthalassa
options.B: The Tethys Sea or Tethys Ocean
options.C: The Atlantic Ocean
options.D: The Pacific Ocean

questions.explanation: The Tethys Sea or Tethys Ocean lay between Laurasia and Gondwanaland in simplified reconstructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What was Gondwanaland?

options.A: The northern major continental assemblage
options.B: The southern major continental assemblage associated with Pangaea
options.C: The ocean surrounding Pangaea
options.D: A mountain belt in North America

questions.explanation: Gondwanaland, usually called Gondwana in modern geological writing, was the southern major continental assemblage associated with Pangaea. It included the landmasses that later became South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia and the Indian subcontinent, together with other fragments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which present-day regions were part of Gondwana?

options.A: North America and Europe
options.B: Africa, South America, Antarctica, Australia, the Indian subcontinent and several smaller continental fragments
options.C: Only Africa and South America
options.D: Only Australia and Antarctica

questions.explanation: Africa, South America, Antarctica, Australia, the Indian subcontinent and several smaller continental fragments were part of Gondwana.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the significance of India being part of Gondwana?

options.A: India never moved after separation
options.B: The Indian landmass was once connected to other Gondwana fragments; it later separated, moved northwards across the Neo-Tethys oceanic region and collided with Eurasia, contributing to the formation and uplift of the Himalayas
options.C: India was always part of Laurasia
options.D: India was the centre of Pangaea

questions.explanation: The Indian landmass was once connected to other Gondwana fragments. It later separated, moved northwards across the Neo-Tethys oceanic region and collided with Eurasia, contributing to the formation and uplift of the Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between Gondwana and Gondwanaland?

options.A: They are completely different landmasses
options.B: They refer broadly to the same southern continental assemblage; 'Gondwana' is the commonly used modern geological term and 'Gondwanaland' remains common in educational texts
options.C: Gondwana is northern and Gondwanaland is southern
options.D: Gondwana is an ocean and Gondwanaland is a continent

questions.explanation: They refer broadly to the same southern continental assemblage. 'Gondwana' is the commonly used modern geological term; 'Gondwanaland' remains common in educational texts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the jigsaw-fit evidence for continental drift?

options.A: The outlines of some continental margins appear to fit together like pieces of a jigsaw puzzle
options.B: Fossils are found on all continents
options.C: All continents have the same climate
options.D: Earthquakes occur only at plate boundaries

questions.explanation: The outlines of some continental margins appear to fit together like pieces of a jigsaw puzzle. The best-known example is the fit between the eastern margin of South America and the western margin of Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the best-known example of jigsaw fit between continents?

options.A: Europe and Asia
options.B: The eastern margin of South America and the western margin of Africa
options.C: Australia and Antarctica
options.D: North America and Europe

questions.explanation: The best-known example is the fit between the eastern margin of South America and the western margin of Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are continental shelves often used instead of modern coastlines for jigsaw-fit comparison?

options.A: Modern coastlines are always straight
options.B: Modern coastlines change with sea level, erosion and deposition; the edges of continental shelves provide a more meaningful approximation of the continental margins
options.C: Continental shelves are easier to see
options.D: Modern coastlines do not exist

questions.explanation: Modern coastlines change with sea level, erosion and deposition. The edges of continental shelves, especially near the 1,000-metre bathymetric contour in classic comparisons, provide a more meaningful approximation of the continental margins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Does the apparent fit of continents alone prove the theory of continental drift?

options.A: Yes, it is conclusive proof
options.B: No, it is suggestive evidence, but it becomes much stronger when combined with fossil, geological and palaeoclimatic matches
options.C: No, it is completely irrelevant
options.D: Yes, because coastlines never change

questions.explanation: No. It is suggestive evidence, but it becomes much stronger when combined with fossil, geological and palaeoclimatic matches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the geological evidence for continental drift?

options.A: Only the study of modern earthquakes
options.B: Rock formations, mountain belts and geological structures of similar age and character occur on continents now separated by oceans; when reconstructed, some of these belts appear to continue across the joined landmasses
options.C: Only the study of ocean currents
options.D: Only the study of fossils

questions.explanation: Rock formations, mountain belts and geological structures of similar age and character occur on continents now separated by oceans. When the continents are reconstructed into earlier positions, some of these belts appear to continue across the joined landmasses.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Give an example of matching geological structures supporting continental drift.

options.A: The Appalachian mountain belt of eastern North America has geological similarities and structural continuities with mountain belts in parts of the British Isles and Scandinavia when the North Atlantic is closed in reconstructions
options.B: The Himalayas match the Andes
options.C: The Alps match the Rockies
options.D: The Ural mountains match the Atlas mountains

questions.explanation: The Appalachian mountain belt of eastern North America has geological similarities and structural continuities with mountain belts in parts of the British Isles and Scandinavia when the North Atlantic is closed in reconstructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is matching rock evidence important for continental drift?

options.A: It proves that all rocks are the same age
options.B: It suggests that regions now separated by oceans may once have been parts of a connected geological system
options.C: It shows that rocks cannot move
options.D: It proves that oceans are static

questions.explanation: It suggests that regions now separated by oceans may once have been parts of a connected geological system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is fossil evidence supporting continental drift?

options.A: Identical or closely related fossils of land and freshwater organisms have been found on continents now separated by oceans
options.B: All fossils are found only in one continent
options.C: Fossils are found only in oceans
options.D: Fossils prove that continents are fixed

questions.explanation: Identical or closely related fossils of land and freshwater organisms have been found on continents now separated by oceans. Their distribution is easier to explain if those continents were once connected.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the importance of Mesosaurus fossils in continental drift?

options.A: Mesosaurus was a freshwater reptile whose fossils occur in parts of South America and southern Africa; its limited ability to cross a wide saltwater ocean supports the idea that the two regions were once joined
options.B: Mesosaurus was a flying dinosaur found worldwide
options.C: Mesosaurus was a marine mammal found only in the Pacific
options.D: Mesosaurus was a plant fossil found in Europe

questions.explanation: Mesosaurus was a freshwater reptile. Its fossils occur in parts of South America and southern Africa. Its limited ability to cross a wide saltwater ocean supports the idea that the two regions were once joined.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where are Mesosaurus fossils found in classic evidence?

options.A: South America and southern Africa
options.B: Europe and Asia
options.C: Australia and Antarctica
options.D: North America and Greenland

questions.explanation: Mesosaurus fossils occur in parts of South America and southern Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the importance of Glossopteris fossils?

options.A: Glossopteris was a seed fern whose fossils are found across several southern continents, including South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica, supporting the former connection of Gondwana landmasses
options.B: Glossopteris was a freshwater reptile found only in South America
options.C: Glossopteris was a marine animal found only in the Pacific
options.D: Glossopteris was a desert plant found only in Africa

questions.explanation: Glossopteris was a seed fern whose fossils are found across several southern continents, including South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica. This broad distribution supports the former connection of Gondwana landmasses.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: On which continents are Glossopteris fossils found?

options.A: South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica
options.B: North America and Europe only
options.C: Only Africa and South America
options.D: Only Australia and Antarctica

questions.explanation: Glossopteris fossils are found across several southern continents, including South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the importance of Lystrosaurus fossils?

options.A: Fossils of the land-dwelling reptile Lystrosaurus occur in Africa, India and Antarctica, among other Gondwana regions, consistent with those landmasses having been connected
options.B: Lystrosaurus was a marine fish found only in the Atlantic
options.C: Lystrosaurus was a flying bird found worldwide
options.D: Lystrosaurus was a plant found only in Europe

questions.explanation: Fossils of the land-dwelling reptile Lystrosaurus occur in Africa, India and Antarctica, among other Gondwana regions. This distribution is consistent with those landmasses having been connected.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where are Lystrosaurus fossils found in classic evidence?

options.A: Africa, India and Antarctica (also other regions in wider fossil record)
options.B: North America and Europe only
options.C: Only South America and Africa
options.D: Only Australia and Asia

questions.explanation: Lystrosaurus fossils occur in Africa, India and Antarctica, among other Gondwana regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the importance of Cynognathus fossils?

options.A: Cynognathus fossils are found in South America and Africa; the animal was a terrestrial reptile, making a broad ocean barrier an unlikely explanation for its distribution
options.B: Cynognathus was a marine reptile found only in the Pacific
options.C: Cynognathus was a plant found only in Antarctica
options.D: Cynognathus was a bird found worldwide

questions.explanation: Cynognathus fossils are found in South America and Africa. The animal was a terrestrial reptile, making a broad ocean barrier an unlikely explanation for its distribution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where are Cynognathus fossils found?

options.A: South America and Africa
options.B: Europe and Asia
options.C: Australia and Antarctica
options.D: North America and Greenland

questions.explanation: Cynognathus fossils are found in South America and Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which fossil is especially associated with South America and southern Africa?

options.A: Mesosaurus
options.B: Glossopteris
options.C: Lystrosaurus
options.D: Cynognathus

questions.explanation: Mesosaurus fossils occur in parts of South America and southern Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which fossil is a seed fern found across several southern continents?

options.A: Mesosaurus
options.B: Glossopteris
options.C: Lystrosaurus
options.D: Cynognathus

questions.explanation: Glossopteris was a seed fern whose fossils are found across several southern continents, including South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which fossil is a terrestrial reptile found in South America and Africa, making a broad ocean barrier an unlikely explanation for its distribution?

options.A: Mesosaurus
options.B: Glossopteris
options.C: Lystrosaurus
options.D: Cynognathus

questions.explanation: Cynognathus fossils are found in South America and Africa. The animal was a terrestrial reptile, making a broad ocean barrier an unlikely explanation for its distribution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which fossil is a land-dwelling reptile found in Africa, India and Antarctica?

options.A: Mesosaurus
options.B: Glossopteris
options.C: Lystrosaurus
options.D: Cynognathus

questions.explanation: Fossils of the land-dwelling reptile Lystrosaurus occur in Africa, India and Antarctica, among other Gondwana regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is palaeoclimatic evidence?

options.A: Evidence of past climates preserved in rocks, sediments, fossils and landforms, which can reveal that continents occupied different climatic zones in the geological past
options.B: Evidence of modern climate only
options.C: Evidence of future climate
options.D: Evidence of ocean currents only

questions.explanation: Palaeoclimatic evidence is evidence of past climates preserved in rocks, sediments, fossils and landforms. It can reveal that continents occupied different climatic zones in the geological past.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do ancient glacial deposits support continental drift?

options.A: Similar-age glacial deposits and glacial scratch marks (striations) occur across parts of South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica; when reconstructed as Gondwana, the glacial evidence forms a more coherent pattern around a southern ice centre
options.B: Glacial deposits are found only in Antarctica today
options.C: Glacial deposits prove that continents are fixed
options.D: Glacial deposits are found only in the Northern Hemisphere

questions.explanation: Similar-age glacial deposits and glacial scratch marks (striations) occur across parts of South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica. When these continents are reconstructed as Gondwana, the glacial evidence forms a more coherent pattern around a southern ice centre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are glacial striations?

options.A: Scratches or grooves cut into bedrock by rocks embedded in moving glacier ice; their orientations can help reconstruct the direction of past ice movement
options.B: Layers of volcanic ash
options.C: Fossils of marine organisms
options.D: Desert sand dunes

questions.explanation: Glacial striations are scratches or grooves cut into bedrock by rocks embedded in moving glacier ice. Their orientations can help reconstruct the direction of past ice movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do coal deposits provide climatic evidence for continental drift?

options.A: Coal commonly forms from abundant plant material in wet, vegetated environments; coal deposits in regions now cold or otherwise climatically different can indicate that those regions once lay in warmer, humid climatic belts
options.B: Coal forms only in deserts
options.C: Coal forms only in polar regions
options.D: Coal deposits prove that continents never moved

questions.explanation: Coal commonly forms from abundant plant material in wet, vegetated environments. Coal deposits in regions now cold or otherwise climatically different can indicate that those regions once lay in warmer, humid climatic belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How can desert deposits or evaporites be used as evidence for continental drift?

options.A: Ancient dune deposits, evaporites and other climate-sensitive sediments can indicate past arid or warm conditions; their distribution may make more sense when continents are restored to earlier positions
options.B: Evaporites form only in cold climates
options.C: Desert deposits are found only in Antarctica
options.D: Evaporites prove that continents are fixed

questions.explanation: Ancient dune deposits, evaporites and other climate-sensitive sediments can indicate past arid or warm conditions. Their distribution may make more sense when continents are restored to earlier positions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the significance of matching placer deposits or mineral belts for continental drift?

options.A: Some mineral deposits and geological provinces on opposite sides of oceans show similarities that can be interpreted as parts of once-connected regions, although they require detailed geological correlation
options.B: They prove that all minerals are the same age
options.C: They are found only in one continent
options.D: They prove that oceans are static

questions.explanation: Some mineral deposits and geological provinces on opposite sides of oceans show similarities that can be interpreted as parts of once-connected regions. These observations can support continental reconstruction, although they require detailed geological correlation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Did Wegener use seafloor magnetic stripes as evidence for continental drift?

options.A: Yes, they were his main evidence
options.B: No, the systematic discovery and interpretation of symmetrical magnetic stripes on the ocean floor came later and helped support seafloor spreading and plate tectonics, not Wegener's original evidence set
options.C: Yes, but only in his later editions
options.D: No, because magnetic stripes do not exist

questions.explanation: No. The systematic discovery and interpretation of symmetrical magnetic stripes on the ocean floor came later and helped support seafloor spreading and plate tectonics, not Wegener's original evidence set.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What later evidence strongly supported continental movement?

options.A: Seafloor spreading at mid-ocean ridges, symmetrical magnetic anomaly stripes, the age pattern of oceanic crust, heat-flow patterns and the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes
options.B: Only the study of modern coastlines
options.C: Only the study of fossils
options.D: Only the study of ancient glaciers

questions.explanation: Seafloor spreading at mid-ocean ridges, symmetrical magnetic anomaly stripes, the age pattern of oceanic crust, heat-flow patterns and the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes provided strong support for moving lithospheric plates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does GPS support modern plate tectonics?

options.A: Satellite geodesy, including GPS measurements, directly measures present-day motion of tectonic plates, commonly at rates of millimetres to centimetres per year
options.B: GPS measures only the depth of the ocean
options.C: GPS proves that plates are stationary
options.D: GPS measures only atmospheric temperature

questions.explanation: Satellite geodesy, including GPS measurements, directly measures present-day motion of tectonic plates, commonly at rates of millimetres to centimetres per year.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What was the main limitation of Wegener's continental drift theory?

options.A: He could not provide a physically convincing mechanism or adequate forces to explain how continents could move over or through the oceanic crust
options.B: He had no fossil evidence
options.C: He had no jigsaw-fit evidence
options.D: He claimed continents never moved

questions.explanation: Wegener could not provide a physically convincing mechanism or adequate forces to explain how continents could move over or through the oceanic crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which forces did Wegener suggest as possible drivers of continental drift?

options.A: Slab pull and ridge push
options.B: Pole-fleeing force related to Earth's rotation and tidal drag associated with the gravitational attraction of the Moon and Sun
options.C: Mantle convection and basal traction
options.D: Solar wind and cosmic rays

questions.explanation: He discussed pole-fleeing force related to Earth's rotation and tidal drag associated with the gravitational attraction of the Moon and Sun. These proposed forces are far too weak to drive continental motion at the required rates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why was the idea of continents ploughing through oceanic crust criticised?

options.A: Oceanic crust is strong and mechanically connected to the lithosphere; a continent could not simply bulldoze its way through the ocean floor without producing deformation and resistance inconsistent with Wegener's proposed mechanism
options.B: Because continents are too light to move
options.C: Because oceanic crust does not exist
options.D: Because continents are fixed

questions.explanation: Oceanic crust is strong and mechanically connected to the lithosphere. A continent could not simply bulldoze its way through the ocean floor without producing deformation and resistance inconsistent with the mechanism Wegener proposed.

options.B: He explained ocean basins perfectly
options.C: He did not study oceans at all
options.D: He claimed oceans do not exist

questions.explanation: His model did not correctly explain the creation and destruction of oceanic crust, the formation of mid-ocean ridges and trenches, or the systematic development of ocean basins.

options.B: Earthquakes and volcanoes do not exist
options.C: Wegener explained them perfectly
options.D: They occur only in the ocean

questions.explanation: Wegener's model did not provide a complete, unified explanation for the narrow belts of earthquakes and volcanoes associated with plate boundaries, especially subduction zones and transform faults.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Was all of Wegener's evidence wrong?

options.A: Yes, all his evidence was wrong
options.B: No, many of his observations and reconstructions were important and broadly correct; the major weakness was the lack of a valid driving mechanism and an incomplete account of ocean-floor processes
options.C: He had no evidence at all
options.D: His evidence was completely ignored

questions.explanation: No. Many of his observations and reconstructions were important and broadly correct. The major weakness was the lack of a valid driving mechanism and an incomplete account of ocean-floor processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How did modern plate tectonics overcome the limitations of Wegener's theory?

options.A: It treats continents and ocean floors as parts of moving lithospheric plates, with plate motion related to mantle dynamics and forces including slab pull and ridge push, explaining seafloor spreading, subduction, earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building
options.B: It rejected all of Wegener's evidence
options.C: It claimed continents are fixed
options.D: It relied only on fossil evidence

questions.explanation: It treats continents and ocean floors as parts of moving lithospheric plates. Plate motion is related to mantle dynamics and forces acting on plates, including slab pull and ridge push, within a complex system. It explains seafloor spreading, subduction, earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is slab pull?

options.A: A force associated with a cold, dense oceanic lithospheric plate sinking into the mantle at a subduction zone and pulling the rest of the plate behind it; widely considered an important driver of plate motion
options.B: The force of magma pushing plates apart at mid-ocean ridges
options.C: The gravitational attraction of the Moon on continents
options.D: The force of Earth's rotation on continents

questions.explanation: Slab pull is a force associated with a cold, dense oceanic lithospheric plate sinking into the mantle at a subduction zone and pulling the rest of the plate behind it. It is widely considered an important driver of plate motion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is ridge push?

options.A: The gravitational force component associated with the elevated mid-ocean ridge, tending to move lithosphere away from the ridge
options.B: A literal sideways push by molten rock
options.C: The force of subducting plates
options.D: The force of tides on continents

questions.explanation: Ridge push is the gravitational force component associated with the elevated mid-ocean ridge, tending to move lithosphere away from the ridge. The term describes a plate-driving force, not a literal sideways push by molten rock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Does mantle convection alone explain all plate motion?

options.B: No, mantle flow and plate motion are coupled, and modern explanations include several forces; slab pull, ridge-related gravitational forces, basal tractions and the resistance of plate boundaries all contribute in varying proportions
options.C: No, plate motion is not related to mantle convection at all
options.D: Yes, but only for oceanic plates

questions.explanation: No. Mantle flow and plate motion are coupled, and modern explanations include several forces. Slab pull, ridge-related gravitational forces, basal tractions and the resistance of plate boundaries all contribute in varying proportions.

questions.explanation: Coal deposits in regions now cold or otherwise climatically different can indicate that those regions once lay in warmer, humid climatic belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a force suggested by Wegener as a possible driver of continental drift?

options.A: Pole-fleeing force
options.B: Tidal drag
options.C: Slab pull
options.D: All of the above were suggested by Wegener

questions.explanation: Wegener suggested pole-fleeing force and tidal drag. Slab pull is a modern concept, not one Wegener proposed.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a modern plate-driving force?

options.A: Pole-fleeing force
options.B: Tidal drag
options.C: Slab pull
options.D: Lunar gravity

questions.explanation: Slab pull is a modern plate-driving force. Pole-fleeing force and tidal drag were Wegener's proposed mechanisms and are not accepted as sufficient drivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is true about mantle convection and plate motion?

options.A: Mantle convection alone explains all plate motion
options.B: Mantle flow and plate motion are coupled, and several forces contribute in varying proportions
options.C: Mantle convection is unrelated to plate motion
options.D: Plate motion is driven only by tidal drag

questions.explanation: Mantle flow and plate motion are coupled, and modern explanations include several forces. Slab pull, ridge-related gravitational forces, basal tractions and the resistance of plate boundaries all contribute in varying proportions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's continental drift and modern plate tectonics?

options.A: Wegener proposed continental drift; modern plate tectonics was developed later and explains both continental and oceanic movement
options.B: Wegener proposed plate tectonics; modern continental drift was developed later
options.C: Both were proposed by Wegener
options.D: Both were proposed by Harry Hess

questions.explanation: Wegener proposed continental drift; modern plate tectonics was developed later and explains both continental and oceanic movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the fit between South America and Africa?

options.A: The eastern margin of South America fits the western margin of Africa
options.B: The western margin of South America fits the eastern margin of Africa
options.C: The northern margin of South America fits the southern margin of Africa
options.D: The southern margin of South America fits the northern margin of Africa

questions.explanation: The best-known example is the fit between the eastern margin of South America and the western margin of Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which bathymetric contour is often used in classic comparisons of continental margins for jigsaw fit?

options.A: The 1,000-metre bathymetric contour
options.B: The 100-metre bathymetric contour
options.C: The 5,000-metre bathymetric contour
options.D: The 10,000-metre bathymetric contour

questions.explanation: The edges of continental shelves, especially near the 1,000-metre bathymetric contour in classic comparisons, provide a more meaningful approximation of the continental margins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the breakup of Pangaea?

options.A: It was a prolonged process rather than a single event
options.B: It happened in a single day
options.C: It has not yet begun
options.D: It occurred only during the Precambrian

questions.explanation: The breakup of Pangaea was a prolonged process rather than a single event.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Tethys Sea?

options.A: A major oceanic seaway located between the northern Laurasian and southern Gondwanan landmasses in standard reconstructions
options.B: The ocean surrounding all of Pangaea
options.C: A supercontinent
options.D: A mountain range

questions.explanation: The Tethys was a major oceanic seaway located between the northern Laurasian and southern Gondwanan landmasses in standard reconstructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Tethys Sea is the predecessor oceanic realm associated with which later mountain building?

options.A: Alpine-Himalayan mountain building
options.B: Appalachian mountain building
options.C: Ural mountain building
options.D: Andean mountain building

questions.explanation: The Tethys Sea is the predecessor oceanic realm associated with later Alpine-Himalayan mountain building.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the scientific status of Wegener's continental drift theory?

options.A: Historically important hypothesis; mechanism rejected, but many observations broadly correct
options.B: Accepted overarching theory in modern Earth science
options.C: Completely false with no correct observations
options.D: Still the only accepted theory

questions.explanation: Wegener's continental drift is a historically important hypothesis; its mechanism was rejected. Many of his observations and reconstructions were important and broadly correct.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the scientific status of modern plate tectonics?

options.A: Accepted overarching theory in modern Earth science
options.B: Historically important hypothesis with a rejected mechanism
options.C: Completely false
options.D: Still debated as to whether plates move

questions.explanation: Modern plate tectonics is the accepted overarching theory in modern Earth science.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes in modern plate tectonics?

options.A: They are concentrated at plate boundaries
options.B: They occur randomly across the globe
options.C: They occur only in the ocean
options.D: They occur only on continents

questions.explanation: Modern plate tectonics explains the concentration of earthquakes and volcanoes at plate boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the age pattern of oceanic crust in the context of plate tectonics?

options.A: Oceanic crust is youngest at mid-ocean ridges and older away from them
options.B: Oceanic crust is the same age everywhere
options.C: Oceanic crust is oldest at mid-ocean ridges
options.D: Oceanic crust does not exist

questions.explanation: The age pattern of oceanic crust, with youngest crust at mid-ocean ridges and older crust away from them, supports seafloor spreading and plate tectonics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's proposed forces and modern accepted forces?

options.A: Wegener's proposed forces are far too weak; modern accepted forces include slab pull and ridge push
options.B: Wegener's proposed forces are the same as modern accepted forces
options.C: Wegener proposed slab pull and ridge push
options.D: Modern plate tectonics has no driving forces

questions.explanation: Wegener's proposed forces (pole-fleeing force and tidal drag) are far too weak to drive continental motion at the required rates. Modern accepted forces include slab pull and ridge push.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of basal tractions in plate motion?

options.A: They contribute along with slab pull, ridge-related gravitational forces and the resistance of plate boundaries in varying proportions
options.B: They are the only force driving plate motion
options.C: They do not exist
options.D: They are the same as tidal drag

questions.explanation: Slab pull, ridge-related gravitational forces, basal tractions and the resistance of plate boundaries all contribute in varying proportions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Pangaea and earlier supercontinents?

options.A: Pangaea was one of several supercontinents; earlier ones include Rodinia and Columbia/Nuna
options.B: Pangaea was the only supercontinent ever
options.C: Pangaea existed before Rodinia
options.D: Rodinia and Columbia are the same as Pangaea

questions.explanation: Geological evidence indicates that earlier supercontinents existed, including Rodinia and Columbia/Nuna. Pangaea is especially important in school-level continental-drift study.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Gondwana and Gondwanaland?

options.A: They refer broadly to the same southern continental assemblage; Gondwana is the modern geological term
options.B: They are completely different landmasses
options.C: Gondwana is northern and Gondwanaland is southern
options.D: Gondwana is an ocean and Gondwanaland is a continent

questions.explanation: They refer broadly to the same southern continental assemblage. 'Gondwana' is the commonly used modern geological term; 'Gondwanaland' remains common in educational texts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Laurasia and Gondwana?

options.A: Laurasia was the northern assemblage; Gondwana was the southern assemblage
options.B: Laurasia was the southern assemblage; Gondwana was the northern assemblage
options.C: Both were northern assemblages
options.D: Both were oceans

questions.explanation: Laurasia was the northern assemblage; Gondwana was the southern assemblage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Pangaea and Panthalassa?

options.A: Pangaea was the supercontinent; Panthalassa was the vast ocean surrounding it
options.B: Pangaea was the ocean; Panthalassa was the supercontinent
options.C: Both were supercontinents
options.D: Both were oceans

questions.explanation: Pangaea was the supercontinent; Panthalassa was the vast ocean surrounding it.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Tethys Sea and Panthalassa?

options.A: Panthalassa surrounded Pangaea; the Tethys lay between Laurasia and Gondwana
options.B: The Tethys surrounded Pangaea; Panthalassa lay between Laurasia and Gondwana
options.C: They are the same
options.D: Both were supercontinents

questions.explanation: Panthalassa was the enormous ocean surrounding Pangaea. The Tethys was a major oceanic seaway located between the northern Laurasian and southern Gondwanan landmasses in standard reconstructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Pacific Ocean and Panthalassa?

options.A: The Pacific is commonly described as the principal remnant of Panthalassa, though modern oceanic crust and boundaries have been extensively renewed
options.B: The Pacific is the same as Panthalassa without any change
options.C: The Pacific is unrelated to Panthalassa
options.D: Panthalassa is a remnant of the Pacific

questions.explanation: The Pacific is commonly described as the principal remnant of Panthalassa, but modern oceanic crust and boundaries have been extensively renewed.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the evidence he assembled?

options.A: No single observation alone proves continental drift; the combined pattern of evidence was the strength of the argument
options.B: Only one piece of evidence was needed
options.C: Wegener had no evidence
options.D: All evidence was found after Wegener's death

questions.explanation: Wegener assembled several independent lines of evidence. No single observation alone proves continental drift; their combined pattern was the strength of the argument.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between continental drift and plate tectonics regarding the ocean floor?

options.A: Wegener did not adequately explain the creation and destruction of the ocean floor; modern plate tectonics explains seafloor spreading and subduction
options.B: Wegener explained seafloor spreading perfectly
options.C: Modern plate tectonics does not study the ocean floor
options.D: Both ignored the ocean floor

questions.explanation: Wegener did not adequately explain the creation and destruction of the ocean floor. Modern plate tectonics explains seafloor spreading and subduction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between continental drift and plate tectonics regarding earthquakes and volcanoes?

options.A: Wegener had no complete unified boundary model; modern plate tectonics explains their concentration at plate boundaries
options.B: Wegener explained them perfectly
options.C: Modern plate tectonics does not study earthquakes
options.D: Both ignored earthquakes and volcanoes

questions.explanation: Wegener had no complete unified boundary model. Modern plate tectonics explains the concentration of earthquakes and volcanoes at plate boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between continental drift and plate tectonics regarding the driving mechanism?

options.A: Wegener's proposed forces were inadequate; modern plate tectonics explains motion through plate forces and mantle-lithosphere dynamics
options.B: Wegener's mechanism was fully correct
options.C: Modern plate tectonics has no driving mechanism
options.D: Both rely on tidal drag

questions.explanation: Wegener's proposed forces were inadequate. Modern plate tectonics explains motion through plate forces and mantle-lithosphere dynamics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between continental drift and plate tectonics regarding the main idea?

options.A: Wegener's continental drift: continents move relative to one another; modern plate tectonics: lithospheric plates move and include both continental and oceanic crust
options.B: Both have the same main idea
options.C: Wegener's theory: plates move; modern plate tectonics: continents move
options.D: Neither involves movement

questions.explanation: In Wegener's continental drift, the main idea is that continents move relative to one another. Modern plate tectonics holds that lithospheric plates move and include both continental and oceanic crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the historical development of Wegener's continental drift and modern plate tectonics?

options.A: Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912 with his book published in 1915; modern plate tectonics was developed mainly in the 1960s from multiple lines of evidence
options.B: Both were developed in the 1960s
options.C: Plate tectonics was proposed in 1912 and continental drift in the 1960s
options.D: Both were proposed in the 19th century

questions.explanation: Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912; his book was published in 1915. Modern plate tectonics was developed mainly in the 1960s from multiple lines of evidence.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the breakup of Pangaea and the formation of Laurasia and Gondwana?

options.A: As Pangaea fragmented, Laurasia formed in the north and Gondwanaland in the south
options.B: Laurasia and Gondwana formed before Pangaea
options.C: Laurasia and Gondwana are the same landmass
options.D: Pangaea formed from the collision of Laurasia and Gondwana

questions.explanation: The northern landmass was Laurasia and the southern landmass was Gondwanaland (also called Gondwana).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between rifting and the breakup of Pangaea?

options.A: Rifting and extension fractured the supercontinent; the opening of new ocean basins and seafloor spreading progressively separated the continental fragments
options.B: Rifting had no role in the breakup
options.C: The breakup occurred without any rifting
options.D: Rifting caused the formation of Pangaea

questions.explanation: Rifting and extension fractured the supercontinent. The opening of new ocean basins and seafloor spreading progressively separated the continental fragments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of Glossopteris fossils?

options.A: South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica
options.B: North America and Europe only
options.C: Only Africa and South America
options.D: Only Australia and Antarctica

questions.explanation: Glossopteris fossils are found across several southern continents, including South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of Lystrosaurus fossils?

options.A: Africa, India and Antarctica (also other regions in wider fossil record)
options.B: North America and Europe only
options.C: Only South America and Africa
options.D: Only Australia and Asia

questions.explanation: Lystrosaurus fossils occur in Africa, India and Antarctica, among other Gondwana regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of Cynognathus fossils?

options.A: South America and Africa
options.B: Europe and Asia
options.C: Australia and Antarctica
options.D: North America and Greenland

questions.explanation: Cynognathus fossils are found in South America and Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of Mesosaurus fossils?

options.A: South America and southern Africa
options.B: Europe and Asia
options.C: Australia and Antarctica
options.D: North America and Greenland

questions.explanation: Mesosaurus fossils occur in parts of South America and southern Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of the Appalachian mountain belt in continental drift?

options.A: It has geological similarities and structural continuities with mountain belts in parts of the British Isles and Scandinavia when the North Atlantic is closed
options.B: It matches the Himalayas exactly
options.C: It has no geological similarities with any other region
options.D: It is located in South America

questions.explanation: The Appalachian mountain belt of eastern North America has geological similarities and structural continuities with mountain belts in parts of the British Isles and Scandinavia when the North Atlantic is closed in reconstructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of glacial striations in continental drift?

options.A: Their orientations can help reconstruct the direction of past ice movement, supporting the reconstruction of Gondwana
options.B: They are fossils of marine organisms
options.C: They are volcanic rocks
options.D: They are desert sand dunes

questions.explanation: Glacial striations are scratches or grooves cut into bedrock by rocks embedded in moving glacier ice. Their orientations can help reconstruct the direction of past ice movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of coal deposits in continental drift?

options.A: Coal deposits in regions now cold or otherwise climatically different can indicate that those regions once lay in warmer, humid climatic belts
options.B: Coal forms only in deserts
options.C: Coal forms only in polar regions
options.D: Coal deposits prove that continents never moved

questions.explanation: Coal commonly forms from abundant plant material in wet, vegetated environments. Coal deposits in regions now cold or otherwise climatically different can indicate that those regions once lay in warmer, humid climatic belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of evaporites in continental drift?

options.A: Ancient dune deposits, evaporites and other climate-sensitive sediments can indicate past arid or warm conditions; their distribution may make more sense when continents are restored to earlier positions
options.B: Evaporites form only in cold climates
options.C: Evaporites are found only in Antarctica
options.D: Evaporites prove that continents are fixed

questions.explanation: Ancient dune deposits, evaporites and other climate-sensitive sediments can indicate past arid or warm conditions. Their distribution may make more sense when continents are restored to earlier positions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of matching placer deposits or mineral belts in continental drift?

options.A: Some mineral deposits and geological provinces on opposite sides of oceans show similarities that can be interpreted as parts of once-connected regions, although they require detailed geological correlation
options.B: They prove that all minerals are the same age
options.C: They are found only in one continent
options.D: They prove that oceans are static

questions.explanation: Some mineral deposits and geological provinces on opposite sides of oceans show similarities that can be interpreted as parts of once-connected regions. These observations can support continental reconstruction, although they require detailed geological correlation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and seafloor magnetic stripes?

options.A: Wegener did not use seafloor magnetic stripes; their discovery and interpretation came later and helped support seafloor spreading and plate tectonics
options.B: Seafloor magnetic stripes were Wegener's main evidence
options.C: Wegener discovered seafloor magnetic stripes
options.D: Seafloor magnetic stripes do not exist

questions.explanation: No. The systematic discovery and interpretation of symmetrical magnetic stripes on the ocean floor came later and helped support seafloor spreading and plate tectonics, not Wegener's original evidence set.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and GPS?

options.A: GPS is later evidence supporting plate tectonics; it directly measures present-day motion of tectonic plates
options.B: GPS was used by Wegener as his main evidence
options.C: GPS proves that plates are stationary
options.D: GPS measures only atmospheric temperature

questions.explanation: Satellite geodesy, including GPS measurements, directly measures present-day motion of tectonic plates, commonly at rates of millimetres to centimetres per year. GPS is later evidence supporting plate tectonics, not original evidence assembled by Wegener.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the age pattern of oceanic crust?

options.A: The age pattern of oceanic crust is later evidence supporting plate tectonics, not original evidence assembled by Wegener
options.B: Wegener used the age pattern of oceanic crust as his main evidence
options.C: The age pattern of oceanic crust proves that continents are fixed
options.D: The age pattern of oceanic crust does not exist

questions.explanation: The age pattern of oceanic crust is later evidence supporting plate tectonics, not original evidence assembled by Wegener.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and heat-flow patterns?

options.A: Heat-flow patterns are later evidence supporting plate tectonics, not original evidence assembled by Wegener
options.B: Wegener used heat-flow patterns as his main evidence
options.C: Heat-flow patterns prove that continents are fixed
options.D: Heat-flow patterns do not exist

questions.explanation: Heat-flow patterns are later evidence supporting plate tectonics, not original evidence assembled by Wegener.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes?

options.A: The global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes is later evidence supporting plate tectonics; Wegener's model did not provide a complete, unified explanation for their narrow belts
options.B: Wegener explained the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes perfectly
options.C: Earthquakes and volcanoes do not exist
options.D: They occur only in the ocean

questions.explanation: Wegener's model did not provide a complete, unified explanation for the narrow belts of earthquakes and volcanoes associated with plate boundaries. The global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes provided strong support for moving lithospheric plates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the formation of mid-ocean ridges and trenches?

options.A: Wegener's model did not correctly explain the formation of mid-ocean ridges and trenches; modern plate tectonics does
options.B: Wegener explained the formation of mid-ocean ridges and trenches perfectly
options.C: Mid-ocean ridges and trenches do not exist
options.D: They are unrelated to plate tectonics

questions.explanation: Wegener's model did not correctly explain the creation and destruction of oceanic crust, the formation of mid-ocean ridges and trenches, or the systematic development of ocean basins. Modern plate tectonics explains these features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the systematic development of ocean basins?

options.A: Wegener's model did not correctly explain the systematic development of ocean basins; modern plate tectonics does
options.B: Wegener explained the systematic development of ocean basins perfectly
options.C: Ocean basins do not exist
options.D: Ocean basins are unrelated to plate tectonics

questions.explanation: Wegener's model did not correctly explain the creation and destruction of oceanic crust, the formation of mid-ocean ridges and trenches, or the systematic development of ocean basins. Modern plate tectonics explains these features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the concept of continents ploughing through oceanic crust?

options.A: The idea was criticised because oceanic crust is strong and mechanically connected to the lithosphere; a continent could not simply bulldoze its way through the ocean floor without producing deformation and resistance inconsistent with Wegener's proposed mechanism
options.B: The idea was universally accepted
options.C: Oceanic crust is weak and easily displaced
options.D: Continents do not move

questions.explanation: Oceanic crust is strong and mechanically connected to the lithosphere. A continent could not simply bulldoze its way through the ocean floor without producing deformation and resistance inconsistent with the mechanism Wegener proposed.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's proposed forces and the required rates of continental motion?

options.A: Wegener's proposed forces are far too weak to drive continental motion at the required rates
options.B: Wegener's proposed forces are strong enough to drive continental motion
options.C: Wegener proposed no forces
options.D: The required rates are zero

questions.explanation: Wegener discussed pole-fleeing force related to Earth's rotation and tidal drag associated with the gravitational attraction of the Moon and Sun. These proposed forces are far too weak to drive continental motion at the required rates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the evidence for continental drift?

options.A: Many of Wegener's observations and reconstructions were important and broadly correct, but the major weakness was the lack of a valid driving mechanism and an incomplete account of ocean-floor processes
options.B: All of Wegener's evidence was wrong
options.C: Wegener had no evidence
options.D: Wegener's evidence was completely ignored

questions.explanation: No. Many of his observations and reconstructions were important and broadly correct. The major weakness was the lack of a valid driving mechanism and an incomplete account of ocean-floor processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between modern plate tectonics and the limitations of Wegener's theory?

options.A: Modern plate tectonics treats continents and ocean floors as parts of moving lithospheric plates, with plate motion related to mantle dynamics and forces including slab pull and ridge push, explaining seafloor spreading, subduction, earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building
options.B: Modern plate tectonics rejected all of Wegener's evidence
options.C: Modern plate tectonics claimed continents are fixed
options.D: Modern plate tectonics relied only on fossil evidence

questions.explanation: Modern plate tectonics treats continents and ocean floors as parts of moving lithospheric plates. Plate motion is related to mantle dynamics and forces acting on plates, including slab pull and ridge push, within a complex system. It explains seafloor spreading, subduction, earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes slab pull?

options.A: A force associated with a cold, dense oceanic lithospheric plate sinking into the mantle at a subduction zone and pulling the rest of the plate behind it
options.B: The force of magma pushing plates apart at mid-ocean ridges
options.C: The gravitational attraction of the Moon on continents
options.D: The force of Earth's rotation on continents

questions.explanation: Slab pull is a force associated with a cold, dense oceanic lithospheric plate sinking into the mantle at a subduction zone and pulling the rest of the plate behind it. It is widely considered an important driver of plate motion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes ridge push?

options.A: The gravitational force component associated with the elevated mid-ocean ridge, tending to move lithosphere away from the ridge
options.B: A literal sideways push by molten rock
options.C: The force of subducting plates
options.D: The force of tides on continents

questions.explanation: Ridge push is the gravitational force component associated with the elevated mid-ocean ridge, tending to move lithosphere away from the ridge. The term describes a plate-driving force, not a literal sideways push by molten rock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between mantle convection and plate motion?

options.A: Mantle flow and plate motion are coupled, and modern explanations include several forces; slab pull, ridge-related gravitational forces, basal tractions and the resistance of plate boundaries all contribute in varying proportions
options.B: Mantle convection alone explains all plate motion
options.C: Mantle convection is unrelated to plate motion
options.D: Plate motion is driven only by tidal drag

questions.explanation: Mantle flow and plate motion are coupled, and modern explanations include several forces. Slab pull, ridge-related gravitational forces, basal tractions and the resistance of plate boundaries all contribute in varying proportions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the main ideas of Wegener's continental drift and modern plate tectonics?

options.A: Wegener's continental drift: continents move relative to one another; modern plate tectonics: lithospheric plates move and include both continental and oceanic crust
options.B: Both have the same main idea
options.C: Wegener's theory: plates move; modern plate tectonics: continents move
options.D: Neither involves movement

questions.explanation: In Wegener's continental drift, the main idea is that continents move relative to one another. Modern plate tectonics holds that lithospheric plates move and include both continental and oceanic crust.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the ocean floor?

options.A: Wegener did not adequately explain the creation and destruction of the ocean floor; modern plate tectonics explains seafloor spreading and subduction
options.B: Wegener explained seafloor spreading perfectly
options.C: Modern plate tectonics does not study the ocean floor
options.D: Both ignored the ocean floor

questions.explanation: Wegener did not adequately explain the creation and destruction of the ocean floor. Modern plate tectonics explains seafloor spreading and subduction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and earthquakes and volcanoes?

options.A: Wegener had no complete unified boundary model; modern plate tectonics explains their concentration at plate boundaries
options.B: Wegener explained them perfectly
options.C: Modern plate tectonics does not study earthquakes
options.D: Both ignored earthquakes and volcanoes

questions.explanation: Wegener had no complete unified boundary model. Modern plate tectonics explains the concentration of earthquakes and volcanoes at plate boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Wegener's theory and the driving mechanism?

options.A: Wegener's proposed forces were inadequate; modern plate tectonics explains motion through plate forces and mantle-lithosphere dynamics
options.B: Wegener's mechanism was fully correct
options.C: Modern plate tectonics has no driving mechanism
options.D: Both rely on tidal drag

questions.explanation: Wegener's proposed forces were inadequate. Modern plate tectonics explains motion through plate forces and mantle-lithosphere dynamics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the scientific status of Wegener's continental drift theory?

options.A: Historically important hypothesis; mechanism rejected, but many observations broadly correct
options.B: Accepted overarching theory in modern Earth science
options.C: Completely false with no correct observations
options.D: Still the only accepted theory

questions.explanation: Wegener's continental drift is a historically important hypothesis; its mechanism was rejected. Many of his observations and reconstructions were important and broadly correct.
